```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r model-load, include = FALSE}
mod <- readModelDb("MartinCerezuela_2024_isavuconazole")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics13080706> (PMC11350865; open
  access, CC BY)
* Preprint: <https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-4027011/v1> (Research Square)

Martin-Cerezuela and colleagues followed 24 critically ill adults in a Spanish
medical intensive care unit who received intravenous isavuconazole at the
labelled regimen. They drew three plasma samples per patient (predose, 1 h and
12 h after the infusion) after 48-96 h of treatment and fitted a population PK
model in NONMEM (ADVAN1 TRANS2, FOCE with interaction). A one-compartment model
with first-order elimination described the 71 concentrations. None of the
screened covariates -- including continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT)
and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) -- improved the model, so the
final model has none.

No erratum or correction was found in Europe PMC or on the journal landing page
(checked 2026-10-30).

# Population

```{r population}
data.frame(
  Characteristic = c(
    "Patients / plasma concentrations", "Age (years)", "Male",
    "Body weight (kg)", "SAPS3 score", "Mechanical ventilation", "CRRT", "ECMO",
    "Confirmed fungal infection", "Serum creatinine", "Albumin",
    "ICU mortality"
  ),
  Value = c(
    "24 / 71", "53.2 (SD 16.4)", "17 (70.8%)", "75.1 (SD 12.6)",
    "63 (IQR 57-71.5)", "23 (95.8%)", "8 (33.3%)", "7 (29.1%)",
    "11 (45.8%)", "0.61 (IQR 0.47-0.79)", "2.4 (SD 0.4)", "14 (58.3%)"
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Martin-Cerezuela 2024 Table 1 and Results 3.1.")
```

All patients received 200 mg isavuconazole every 8 h for six doses, then
200 mg every 24 h, each as a 60-min intravenous infusion (Methods 2.1). Of the
confirmed infections, seven were candidemia (six *Candida auris*), two invasive
pulmonary aspergillosis, one *C. parapsilosis* ventriculitis and one
mucormycosis. Race and ethnicity are not reported. The same information is
available as `readModelDb("MartinCerezuela_2024_isavuconazole")()$population`.

# Closed-form check of the typical patient

The paper's Table 2 also prints an AUC of 37.31 mg*h/L, computed "by
determining the total dose and dividing it by the clearance" (Methods 2.2).
That is exactly the 200 mg daily dose divided by the typical clearance
(200 / 5.36 = 37.31), so it is the typical-patient steady-state AUC over one
24-h dosing interval. The typical-value solve below runs the full labelled
regimen for three weeks and checks the last interval against the closed-form
steady-state infusion solution.

```{r regimen}
tau <- 24
t_maint <- 64 # first maintenance dose, 24 h after the sixth loading dose
n_maint <- 21
t_ss <- t_maint + (n_maint - 1) * tau # last maintenance dose

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 168, by = 0.5),
  t_ss + c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24)
)))

make_events <- function(n, id_offset = 0L) {
  rxode2::et(amt = 200, dur = 1, ii = 8, addl = 5, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(
      time = t_maint, amt = 200, dur = 1, ii = tau, addl = n_maint - 1,
      cmt = "central"
    ) |>
    rxode2::et(time = obs_times, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(id = id_offset + seq_len(n)) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = "200 mg q8h x6, then 200 mg q24h")
}
```

```{r closed-form}
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), make_events(1L),
  keep = "regimen", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10
) |>
  as.data.frame()

cl_typ <- exp(ui$theta[["lcl"]])
v_typ <- exp(ui$theta[["lvc"]])
k_typ <- cl_typ / v_typ
r_inf <- 200 / 1 # mg/h over the 1-h infusion

# Steady-state infusion solution over one interval (t = time since dose start)
css <- function(t) {
  acc <- 1 / (1 - exp(-k_typ * tau))
  c_end <- r_inf / cl_typ * (1 - exp(-k_typ * 1)) * acc
  ifelse(
    t <= 1,
    r_inf / cl_typ * (1 - exp(-k_typ * t)) + c_end * exp(-k_typ * (tau - 1)) * exp(-k_typ * t),
    c_end * exp(-k_typ * (t - 1))
  )
}

ss_rows <- typ |> dplyr::filter(time >= t_ss)
rel_err <- abs(ss_rows$Cc / css(ss_rows$time - t_ss) - 1)

auc_ss_typ <- with(ss_rows, sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2))

data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "max relative error, ODE vs closed form (last interval)",
    "AUC0-24,ss by trapezoid (mg*h/L)", "Dose / CL (mg*h/L)",
    "Published AUC, Table 2 (mg*h/L)"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%.1e", max(rel_err)),
    sprintf("%.2f", c(auc_ss_typ, 200 / cl_typ, 37.31))
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # Same drawn (typical) parameters on both sides: pure numerical error.
  max(rel_err) < 1e-5,
  # Transcription: dose / CL reproduces the printed AUC to its 4 digits.
  abs(200 / cl_typ - 37.31) < 0.005,
  # The trapezoid on the 0.25-4 h grid is within 1% of the exact integral.
  abs(auc_ss_typ / 37.31 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation

The cohort has no covariates to draw: the final model has none. 200 patients
receive the labelled regimen used in the study.

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241030)
events <- make_events(200L)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Concentration-time profile over the first week

```{r profile, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
obs_means <- data.frame(
  label = c("Cmin", "Cmax", "C50"),
  time = c(t_maint, t_maint + 2, t_maint + 13),
  Cc = c(1.76, 3.99, 2.26)
)

sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 168) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(data = dplyr::filter(typ, time <= 168), aes(time, Cc), linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(data = obs_means, aes(time, Cc), colour = "firebrick", size = 2.5) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 48, xmax = 96, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.08) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (h)", y = "Isavuconazole Cc (mg/L)",
    title = "Simulated median and 90% interval, typical patient (dashed)",
    caption = paste(
      "Red points: observed means of Cmin, Cmax and C50 (Results 3.2), placed at",
      "the first maintenance dose. Shaded band: the 48-96 h sampling window."
    )
  )
```

## Figure 1 -- sampled concentrations

The study sampled each patient once, at predose (Cmin), 1 h (Cmax) and 12 h
(C50) after completing an infusion, some time between 48 and 96 h of
treatment (Methods 2.2). The regimen puts the first maintenance dose at 64 h
and the second at 88 h, so both fall inside that window; the simulation below
reads both.

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sample_times <- data.frame(
  window = rep(c("1st maintenance dose (64 h)", "2nd maintenance dose (88 h)"), each = 3),
  sample = rep(c("Cmin", "Cmax", "C50"), 2),
  time = c(t_maint + c(0, 2, 13), t_maint + tau + c(0, 2, 13))
)

sampled <- sim |>
  dplyr::inner_join(sample_times, by = "time") |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c("Cmin", "Cmax", "C50")))

ggplot(sampled, aes(sample, Cc)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6) +
  geom_point(
    data = obs_means |> dplyr::mutate(sample = factor(label, levels = levels(sampled$sample))),
    aes(sample, Cc), colour = "firebrick", size = 3, shape = 18
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(1, 5), linetype = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~window) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Isavuconazole Cc (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Martin-Cerezuela 2024. Red diamonds: observed means (Results 3.2); dotted lines: 1-5 mg/L target range."
  )
```

```{r sample-compare}
observed <- data.frame(
  sample = c("Cmin", "Cmax", "C50"),
  obs_mean = c(1.76, 3.99, 2.26),
  obs_sd = c(1.02, 1.96, 1.20)
)

sample_cmp <- sampled |>
  dplyr::group_by(window, sample) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_mean = mean(Cc), sim_sd = sd(Cc),
    pct_below_1 = 100 * mean(Cc < 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = as.character(sample)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(observed, by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_mean / obs_mean - 1))

sample_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(c(sim_mean, sim_sd, obs_mean, obs_sd), \(x) round(x, 2)),
    dplyr::across(c(pct_below_1, pct_diff), \(x) round(x, 1))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(window, sample, obs_mean, obs_sd, sim_mean, sim_sd, pct_diff, pct_below_1) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Sampling window" = window,
    "Sample" = sample,
    "Observed mean (mg/L)" = obs_mean,
    "Observed SD" = obs_sd,
    "Simulated mean (mg/L)" = sim_mean,
    "Simulated SD" = sim_sd,
    "% diff (mean)" = pct_diff,
    "Simulated % below 1 mg/L" = pct_below_1
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Observed (Results 3.2) vs simulated sampled concentrations. 12.5% of observed troughs were below 1 mg/L.")

first_window <- sample_cmp |>
  dplyr::filter(window == "1st maintenance dose (64 h)")
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL, V, dose or infusion time moves every
  # sampled mean by tens of percent. Realised -2 / -20 / -13% for Cmin /
  # Cmax / C50 here; Monte Carlo SE of a 200-subject mean is 2-4%.
  all(abs(first_window$pct_diff) < 35)
)
```

## Figure 2 -- individual clearance and volume

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
indiv <- sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl, vc)

indiv |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cl, vc), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::mutate(parameter = dplyr::recode(
    parameter,
    cl = "Clearance (L/h)", vc = "Volume of distribution (L)"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Compare with Figure 2 of Martin-Cerezuela 2024 (individual CL and V by",
      "ECMO and CRRT status). The model has no ECMO or CRRT effect, so the",
      "simulated distribution is the same for every subgroup."
    )
  )

stopifnot(
  # Realised IIV against the encoded omega (log(1 + CV^2)); SE of an SD from
  # 200 draws is about 5%.
  abs(sd(log(indiv$cl)) / sqrt(ui$omega["etalcl", "etalcl"]) - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(sd(log(indiv$vc)) / sqrt(ui$omega["etalvc", "etalvc"]) - 1) < 0.25
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over the last 24-h dosing interval of the three-week
simulation.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, regimen)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, regimen) |>
  dplyr::mutate(duration = 1)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id,
  route = "intravascular", duration = "duration"
)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = t_ss,
  end = t_ss + tau,
  cmax = TRUE,
  cmin = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  cav = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

The paper's only NCA-type quantity is the AUC in Table 2. It is the typical
patient's dose / CL, which is the population median of the individual
dose / CL values, so it is compared against the median simulated steady-state
AUC0-24 (`ncaComparisonTable()` pools by the median).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- data.frame(regimen = "200 mg q8h x6, then 200 mg q24h", auclast = 37.31)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "regimen",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Steady-state AUC0-24: published (Table 2) vs simulated median.")

auc_ss <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast")
stopifnot(
  # Median of dose / CL_i is dose / CL_typ for a lognormal CL; Monte Carlo
  # SE of the median from 200 subjects is about 4%.
  abs(median(auc_ss$PPORRES) / 37.31 - 1) < 0.15
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Residual error.** Neither the article nor its Research Square preprint
  reports a residual error model or its magnitude. Proportional and additive
  residual SDs are carried as `fixed(0)` rather than invented, so simulations
  from this model show between-subject variability only.
- **IIV scale.** Table 2's `%CV` column (the preprint footnote calls it "percent
  covariance of intersubject-variability") is converted with
  omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1), giving 0.1867 for CL and 0.3708 for V. The paper
  does not say whether its %CV is instead 100 x sqrt(omega^2), which would give
  0.2052 and 0.4489. No confidence interval on the variances is printed, so the
  two readings cannot be separated from the paper; the difference in the SD of
  log(CL) is under 5% and in log(V) about 10%.
- **Table 2 RSE for clearance.** The printed %RSE of 35.7% for clearance does
  not match its own SE (0.576 / 5.36 = 10.7%) or its 95% CI
  (5.36 +/- 1.96 x 0.576 = 4.23-6.49). The point estimate, SE and CI agree,
  so the point estimate is used as printed.
- **Start of maintenance dosing.** Methods 2.1 gives six 200 mg loading doses
  every 8 h followed by 200 mg every 24 h without saying when the first
  maintenance dose falls. The simulation starts it 24 h after the last
  loading dose (at 64 h), the later end of the 12-24 h interval in the
  product label.
- **Sampling times.** Methods 2.2 places Cmax and C50 at 1 h and 12 h "after
  completing the drug infusion" (simulated at 2 h and 13 h after the start of
  the 1-h infusion); the abstract says "after the last dose". The study does
  not say on which day within 48-96 h each patient was sampled, so the first
  two maintenance doses are both shown. Observed means sit closest to the
  first-maintenance-dose window (simulated Cmin within a few percent, Cmax
  about 20% lower); at the second window all three simulated means are
  about 23-28% lower, consistent with most patients having been sampled soon
  after the loading phase.
- **Spread of the simulated concentrations.** With no residual error, the
  simulated concentrations carry between-subject variability only. The
  simulated SD of Cmax (about 1 mg/L) is about half the observed SD
  (1.96 mg/L), and the simulated fraction of troughs below 1 mg/L (about a
  quarter at the first window) is higher than the observed 12.5% (3 of 24),
  which a 24-patient sample estimates only coarsely.
- **Covariate units in Table 1.** Table 1 prints bilirubin in umol/L
  (mean 1.1) and albumin in g/L (mean 2.4); both magnitudes are mg/dL and g/dL
  values. They are documented that way in `covariatesDataExcluded`; no
  covariate enters the model.
- **ECMO and CRRT.** The authors tested both on CL and V and retained neither
  (Results 3.3, Figure 2), so the model applies to patients on and off these
  devices alike.
